versions.changelog:
**golang-popular-libraries v1.2.0 Changelog**

- Added cross-references and workflow integration for the golang-pkg-go-dev ("godig") and golang-gopls skills, offering improved library vetting and comparison.
- Updated compatibility metadata to mention Codex and extended the allowed tools list (including godig, gopls, LSP, and various Context7 actions).
- Enhanced recommendation guidance on leveraging import count and pkg.go.dev metadata for library evaluation.
- Expanded and clarified documentation on best practices for discovering, comparing, and validating Go libraries.
- Removed the deprecated skill-card.md file.

- Made the skill user-invocable (can now be triggered explicitly by users).
- Updated skill description to clarify when recommendations are applied, emphasizing explicit user requests or new dependency additions.
- Bumped version to 1.1.5 in metadata.

- Added AskUserQuestion to allowed tools for enhanced interactive capabilities.
- Updated metadata version to 1.1.4 and made minor text corrections.
- Improved language in documentation and reference links for accuracy and clarity.

- Updated library and tool references for improved accuracy and coverage.
- Added an evals/evals.json file to support evaluation and validation.
- Minor updates to metadata and internal documentation.
- Bumped version to 1.1.2.

- Initial release: recommends production-ready Golang libraries and frameworks for a wide range of use cases.
- Favors standard library solutions when possible; suggests third-party options only if they add clear value.
- Offers structured reference catalogs for libraries, tools, and experimental stdlib packages.
- Outlines best practices, anti-patterns, and evaluation criteria for selecting libraries.
- Designed for seamless integration with Claude Code and similar AI coding agents.
